full_judgment:
judgment and order dated 24.01.2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.5157 of 2000 arising out of an order dated 5.6.2000 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Magura in Criminal Revision No.20 of 2000 directing the Court of Magistrate to proceed with the case bearing No. 1067 of 1999 in accordance with the sub-section (2A) of section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 2. An application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was filed by the petitioner for setting aside the order of dismissal passed by the Court of Magistrate, Magura and to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 5.6.2000 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Magura in Criminal Revision No.20 of 2000 setting aside the order of dismissal dated 06.04.2000 passed by the Court of Magistrate, Magura in Petition Case No.1067 of 1999 and thereupon directing the Court of Magistrate to proceed with the case under sub-section (2A) of section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall not he set aside and the order of the dismissal passed by the Court of Magistrate shall not be upheld. 

 Peace Committee of Baharbag Union in 1971 while the other petitioners were the armed Rajakars of the said committee. The petitioner set up a "Rajakar Camp" near Sattyajir Bazar beside the Baba Ganga river. On 25.10.1971 the petitioners forcibly brought Hashem Mollah. father of the complainant-respondent Nos. 1 and 6 other persons to the said camp and carried on physical torture upon them, ultimately in the midnight of 27.10.1971 the petitioners killed them and thereby committed offence punishable under sections 147/148/149/302 read with section 114 of the Penal Code. The complaint petition contained names of 16 persons so killed along with a list of 34 persons as witnesses. On receipt of the complaint petition containing the aforesaid allegation the Magistrate examined complainant-respondent No. 1 under section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and directed an inquiry into the matter by the Officer-in-Charge of Magura Police Station. On being endorsed by the Officer-in-Charge one Md. Zaiul Alam, a Sub-Inspector of Police, held inquiry into the matter and submitted a report stating that at the instance of one Bagres Khan, Magura Police Station Case No. 12 dated 24.01.1972 was started over the selfsame occurrence against 20 accused persons including petitioner No. 1 and another Sayed Abul Kashem (not a party to the complaint petition). On conclusion of investigation into the said P.S. Case charge-sheet was submitted against petitioner No. 1 and 20 accused persons for the offence punishable under section 302 and 120B of the Penal Code. It was also reported by him that the learned Sessions Judge, Jessore who held the trial acquitted all the accused persons on 4,2.1975. It was further stated in the inquiry report that as a sequel to social rivalry between the parties the complainant respondent No.1 lodged the case as a measure of vengeance on them after lapse of a considerable period of time. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the said order the complainant-respondent No. I preferred a Criminal Revision being No.20 of 2000 tinder section 435 read with section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Learned Sessions .Judge, Magma who heard the revision by his impugned judgment and order dated 5.6.2000 allowed the revision set aside the order of the Magistrate dated 6.4.2000 and directed him to proceed with the case in terms of subsection 2(A) of section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 6. Being aggrieved the petitioners moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Upon hearing the said application the rules was discharged on the finding that:  "...how far the petitioners were competent to prefer the instant application under section 56IA of the Code when cognizance in the case had not yet been taken by the Magistrate. A judicial proceeding cannot be treated to have been started till before cognizance has been taken by the Magistrate. No cognizance having yet been taken against the petitioners they are not competent to challenge the impugned revisional judgment and order or the Sessions Judge who directed a judicial inquiry by setting aside the order of the Magistrate dismissing the complaint petition. That would amount to quashing an inquiry proceeding relating a complaint petition. which discloses an offence, exclusively triable by a Court of Sessions. This is not permissible in law. This not being a judicial proceeding pending after cognizance by a competent Magistrate this Court cannot quash such inquiry proceeding. In a decision in the case of Syed Muhammad Hashem alias Hashim Vs. State reported in 48 DLR (AD) 1996) it has been held by our Lordships of the Appellate Division...." Proceeding before a Court starts when the Magistrate takes cognizance of an offence on police report or on complaint. Before such cognizance, there is no proceeding that may he quashed under section 561 A Cr.P.C." This rule is incompetent." 

 8. It appears from the record that the case was filed over an occurrence of 1971 after lapse of about 25 years and the petitioner alleged that the same is the product of ill motive and to harass because of social rivalry and property dispute existing between the parties but the fact of filing of the case after a lapse of 25 years is no bar to prosecution as there is no period of limitation in lodging of an FIR in respect of a cognizable offence committed by an accused and we do not find any illegality on the part of the learned Sessions Judge to direct for holding judicial enquiry under section 202(2A) of the Code of Criminal Procedure in case of an offence unsuccessfully tried by Court of Sessions Judge upon taking cognizance over the report of the enquiry officer holding an enquiry through a Sub-Inspector of Police in terms of provision of section 202(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The High Court Division also found that the Sessions Judge has not appeared to have passed any Blanquette order directing judicial enquiry when appeared to him that the selfsame police officer who held enquiry twice was influenced by the order of acquittal of the accused petitioner No.1 and others previously.
